title: With an idempotency key, the retry gets the stored response, not a second charge
caption: The client picks the key once per checkout and resends it on every attempt; the server claims it before doing the work.

messages.label: POST /pay $30 · Key: 7f3a
messages.note: The client generates the UUID 7f3a when the user presses Pay, not per attempt.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a (in_progress)
messages.note: The unique key column makes this claim succeed exactly once.

messages.label: charge $30 · key 7f3a
messages.note: The key is passed downstream too, so the processor also dedupes.

messages.label: UPDATE 7f3a: done, 201 {pay_42}
messages.note: The response is stored next to the key.

messages.label: 201 {pay_42} (lost)
messages.note: Same failure as before: the reply never arrives.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a → conflict, row is done
messages.note: The claim fails, and the existing row says the work is finished.

messages.label: 201 {pay_42} (replayed)
messages.note: Byte-for-byte the original response. One charge, and the client can't tell it was a retry.
